Deflate the jammed 154-point optimum by deleting rattlers plus high-contact core points, LP-polish the smaller set to a lower maximum, then regrow one point at a time via large hole search plus single-point refinement and short LP polishes with retry on jumps.
direction: Follow a deflation–regrowth path in the number of points: delete the 11 rattlers together with 19–29 of the highest-contact or highest-dual points, LP-polish the remaining 114–124 points until their maximum is substantially lower, then reinsert points one at a time. For each insertion, choose the best of at least 20,000 random sphere samples by its maximum inner product with the current set, locally refine that single point against the fixed set with tangent softmax descent, insert it, and run a short LP polish over all points (2–4 seconds) before the next insertion. If an insertion causes the polished maximum to jump sharply, retry that slot from the next-best holes or remove an additional neighbouring high-contact point and reinsert both in swapped order; continue to exactly 154 points and finish with the remaining time in LP polish, since passing through lower-\(n\) optima can reorganise the jammed core rather than merely moving free points.

Greedy construction from signed-permutation template pool with randomized tie-breaking plus noise-break and annealed softmax Adam relaxation with selective trust-region LP polishing.
direction: Search from a structured signed-permutation template pool instead of perturbing the incumbent: generate all distinct signed permutations of templates such as \((1,1,0^8)/\sqrt2\), \((1,1,1,0^7)/\sqrt3\), \((2,1,1,0^7)/\sqrt6\), and \((1,1,1,1,0^6)/2\), optionally including a small number of continuously parameterised templates whose nonzero coordinates are randomly sampled and then normalised. For each randomised greedy pass, repeatedly add the pool vector minimising the current maximum inner product (breaking ties by the sum of exponentials of its largest inner products) until 154 points are selected, then break the exact symmetry with tiny noise and LP-polish. Repeat many inexpensive greedy selections with different template mixtures and random tie-breaking, LP-polish only selections whose pre-polish maximum is below about \(0.43\), and keep any polished result that beats \(0.4012522\); this explores algebraically regular, balanced-contact configurations absent from the current asymmetric local optimum.

idea: Portfolio of fresh and large-perturbation basins with brief Riesz/log-sum-exp Adam relaxations, contact-graph fingerprint de-duplication, and post-LP-only acceptance with hard time reserves.
direction: Run a diversity-preserving portfolio of genuinely different basins with post-LP acceptance and hard internal deadlines: generate candidates from fresh random configurations and from large, varied perturbations of the incumbent, optimise each briefly with several Riesz or log-sum-exp energies (for example powers \(p=8,16,32,64\)) rather than only near-max softmax, and fingerprint each candidate by its thresholded contact graph (degree sequence and leading adjacency eigenvalues at slack \(0.005\)). Discard candidates whose fingerprint is nearly identical to the incumbent or to an already-tested candidate, LP-polish only the three to five most promising distinct candidates for at most 8 seconds each, and accept or reject strictly by the polished maximum. Reserve the final 25–30 seconds for polishing the best distinct candidate, enforce an internal cutoff around 165 seconds, and return the incumbent immediately if any LP call or candidate fails, directly addressing both the repeated-basin problem and the recent timeouts.

idea: LP-dual-guided cluster unlocking that selects high-dual 12–18 point connected clusters, kicks them in the Jacobian tangent null space and re-optimises the cluster with penalised softmax before time-capped full LP polish.
direction: Use LP-dual-guided cluster unlocking rather than rattler relocation: run the existing LP polish but retain the final inequality marginals from HiGHS (falling back to contact degree if marginals are unavailable), aggregate their absolute values by point, threshold the contact graph at \(10^{-7}\), and select a connected cluster of 12–18 points with the largest dual mass. Freeze all other points, compute the Jacobian of that cluster’s active contacts, sample several random displacements in its approximate tangent null space with angular sizes \(0.05\)–\(0.15\) radians, and reoptimise only the cluster with a minimax softmax objective plus a temporary penalty preventing its old contacts from returning above \(0.38\). Unfreeze all points, apply a strictly time-capped LP polish (about 6 seconds per cluster), and accept the result only from its post-LP maximum; cycle through several distinct high-dual clusters while always retaining the best fully polished configuration as fallback.

idea: Vertex-cover deflate-regrow plus core-to-hole teleport, orthogonal-block restarts and hemisphere crossover, all judged only after annealed Adam plus bounded LP polish with wandering acceptance.

idea: Temperature-accepted large-kick basin hopping from scratch without intermediate LP to escape the amorphous near-jammed basin, then intensive smooth plus trust-region LP polish of the top pool.
Rigidity-guided soft-mode basin hopping using tangent-space SVD escapes with geodesic steps plus short softmax Adam and LP snap.
direction: Make rigidity-guided soft-mode escapes instead of random point kicks. Recompute contacts using a realistic threshold such as cosine slack $<10^{-6}$ or $<10^{-5}$, build the tangent-space rigidity matrix for those pairs (nine tangent coordinates per point, hence about $154\times9$ variables), and compute its smallest singular vectors or a positive equilibrium stress via a sparse SVD/NNLS calculation. Generate trial configurations by displacing the current code by $0.03$–$0.25$ radians along random combinations of the softest 10–30 modes, optionally flipping signs to reduce the current highest pairs, then run only 300–600 steps of annealed softmax Adam and keep a trial only if its true maximum improves after a short active-set LP. This directly targets motions that preserve most near-contacts while breaking/reforming a small part of the contact graph, and all LP/SVD calls must use an explicit deadline with the incumbent returned if the budget expires.

idea: Wandering-current basin hopping with hemisphere rigid rotations and greedy cap regrowth plus fast Riesz/softmax Adam and push refinement, saving trust-region LP for a final polish to force real topology changes.

Build structured pool (D10 roots, coordinates, sign vectors, sampled signed-permutation orbits) select 154 by greedy plus swap annealing then free Adam, plus cyclic-rotation tied symmetric orbit optimization before symmetry release, keep best and LP polish.
direction: Search algebraic and symmetry-generated constructions rather than perturbing the amorphous incumbent. Build a candidate pool from structured vectors in $\mathbb R^{10}$, including $D_{10}$ roots $(\pm1,\pm1,0^8)/\sqrt2$, coordinate vectors, signed all-ones-type vectors, and signed-permutation orbits of a few parameterized seed patterns such as $(a,a,a,b,b,0^5)$ with $3a^2+2b^2=1$. First choose 154 pool vectors by greedy max-min selection followed by swap-based simulated annealing on an objective such as $\sum_{i<j}\exp(60\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)$, then release the selected vectors into continuous softmax Adam and final LP polishing; separately optimize the parameters of small unions of full signed-permutation orbits before releasing their symmetry. Symmetry would automatically create many exactly equal contacts and may reach a basin inaccessible to local perturbations of the current asymmetric code.

idea: Antipodal reduction to 77 lines optimizing max absolute inner product with multi-start annealed softmax Adam, then symmetry-breaking unrestricted relaxation and capped LP polish.
direction: Test the missing antipodal structure by solving the reduced 77-line packing problem from many independent starts. Represent the code as $X=[Y;-Y]$ with $Y\in\mathbb R^{77\times10}$ unit rows, so the full maximum cosine is $\max_{i<j}|\langle y_i,y_j\rangle|$, and optimize this absolute-Gram objective with batched multi-start annealed softmax Adam over absolute inner products, using at least 16 random starts and retaining several geometrically distinct finalists rather than only the best. Then unfreeze all 154 points, run unrestricted relaxation and a final capped LP polish, and keep the result only if it beats 0.4012521675368. Even if exact antipodality is not optimal, its halved search space and doubled contact structure provide genuinely different starting basins from the incumbent.

idea: Delete-and-regrow homotopy on a BFS contact cluster with Adam relaxation and greedy hole refilling
direction: Use a properly time-budgeted delete-and-regrow homotopy that removes a whole connected cluster, not isolated points. Select a high-degree point under a $10^{-5}$ contact graph, take its breadth-first cluster of 12–24 points, delete that cluster, relax the remaining points with Adam until their maximum drops, and then reinsert points one at a time: for each insertion sample about 20,000 sphere candidates, refine the best few by single-point softmax descent against the frozen configuration, insert the winner, and perform a short all-point relaxation. Repeat insertions until 154 points are restored, checking elapsed time after every insertion and reserving the final 25–30 seconds for one capped active-set LP polish; if any stage exceeds its allotment, abandon the trial and return the best completed configuration. This changes dozens of contacts simultaneously and avoids the previous timeout failure mode of running expensive LP polishes on every intermediate reduced/regrown code.

idea: Antipodal 77-axis search from a structured pool with descending-target hinge-softmax Adam plus greedy hole swaps, then released 154-point anneal and capped LP polish.
direction: Search a genuinely different algebraic basin by imposing antipodal and lattice structure initially: parametrise only 77 unit vectors $y_i$ and set the code to $\{y_i,-y_i\}$, initialise the axes greedily from a structured pool consisting of coordinate vectors, normalised two-support vectors $(\pm e_a\pm e_b)/\sqrt2$, four-support sign vectors, random vectors, and vectors obtained from low-dimensional lattice constructions embedded in $\mathbb R^{10}$. Alternate greedy pool swaps that remove the axis contributing most pairs above the current target with tangent-space softmax optimisation of the 77 axes, using targets descending from $0.42$ toward $0.395$; after the symmetric stage, release all 154 points independently for a shorter annealed relaxation and final capped LP polish. This tests whether the missing structure is an antipodal, highly symmetric contact topology, and even if the symmetric restriction is not itself optimal, releasing it can enter a basin inaccessible from the incumbent.

idea: Fix the snapped LP to include the whole near-jammed plateau and combine corrected trust-region LP with hole-relocation plus low-temperature softmax basin hopping and fresh restarts.
Collective soft-mode escape along nullspace of near-contact Jacobian via svds plus low-temperature softmax Adam and capped trust-region LP.
direction: Perform a collective soft-mode escape from the current optimum rather than point kicks: build the near-contact graph using slack thresholds $10^{-6}$, $10^{-5}$ and $10^{-4}$, parametrise each point by a $10\times9$ tangent basis, assemble the sparse pair Jacobian for pairs with slack below $2\times10^{-5}$, and compute its 20-40 smallest singular directions with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`. Generate trial configurations by moving along random combinations of these soft directions with geodesic step sizes $0.02$, $0.06$, $0.12$ and $0.20$ radians, then run annealed softmax Adam with temperature decreasing from $3\times10^{-3}$ to $2\times10^{-5}$ so the final stage can resolve near-ties, followed by at most 25 seconds of trust-region LP polish. Keep an internal deadline near 160 seconds, test the true maximum after every stage, and always retain the best complete configuration encountered; this directly searches the collective motions that single-point relocation cannot reach.

direction: Implement large delete-and-regrow topology surgery with strict time control and no expensive intermediate LP: remove 18-30 points at once, choosing a connected cluster in the $10^{-5}$-slack contact graph plus several overloaded points, optimise the remaining 124-136 points for a fixed small number of softmax-Adam steps until their maximum falls appreciably, then reinsert deleted points one at a time from 30,000 random sphere candidates scored against the current set, refine each inserted point by 100 single-point softmax steps, and perform 120 global relaxation steps after every five insertions. Repeat with different cluster sizes and random seeds while time permits, reserve only the final 20 seconds for LP polish, check elapsed time at least every 50 iterations, and maintain a valid best $(154,10)$ array throughout so the method cannot repeat the previous deflation timeout.
